_about: The record lifecycle, rehearsed in ONE world: computed -> filed -> lost -> recovered -> retired.
Four tools keep this repo honest and they are a CHAIN, not four islands:
- a VERIFIER computes a verdict on its cron day and posts it to #18 (verify-oct3.ps1);
- the day-after SENTINEL trips when that day's receipt never landed (oct4-sentinel.ps1);
- the HEARTBEAT AUDITOR asks whether a completed run that owed a record recorded it
(heartbeat-audit.mjs);
- the RECOVERY PASS re-posts a record from the run's own artifact before it expires
(recover-verdicts.mjs).
Each tool had its own rehearsal and each rehearsal built its own little world, so the thing
that actually fails in production - a handoff BETWEEN two of them - had nowhere to be
exercised. scripts/rehearse-lifecycle.mjs runs all four against the ONE world declared here
(scripts/rehearse-world.mjs is its only interpreter, in either language) and stops at the
first step whose handoff does not hold.
WHICH CHAIN. This is the Oct 3 chain, because its record went through all five states for
real. The Oct 28 promotion chain is the same shape but not the same story - its verdicts are
NO_DISPATCH_RUN and PRE_PROMO_* before the operator's dispatch, and closing #18 is an
operator act - so its states live in the sentinel rehearsal (both oct29 trip paths and its
clear path) and in the recovery pass's own pins, not here.
THE TIMELINE IS THE REAL ONE, COMPRESSED. The Oct 3 chain really fired three times, really
derived PASS_REFRESHED three times, and really recorded none of it: oct3-verify.yml was the
one workflow posting to #18 without `issues: write`, so every POST came back 403 and every
run exited 0 on the strength of the verdict it had failed to file. The Oct 4 sentinel really
tripped on the morning after. The verdict was really recovered out of the run's artifact -
by hand, six days later, which is why the recovery pass exists. The only liberty taken here
is the clock: the recovery runs hours after the gap is noticed rather than days, because what
is being rehearsed is the HANDOFF (who reads whose output) and not the six days a human took.
THE WORLD IS A SUBSET, DELIBERATELY. `world.workflows` registers the five workflows these four
tools can name - the auditor audits what the API LISTS, and the recovery pass enumerates the
contract's own RECOVERABLE set - but it is not the repo's whole scheduled fleet, and it gives
no runs to the chains whose days have not arrived (their slots are simply not yet due). The
seeded facts are the real ones where the chain HAS already happened -
run 37123382655 is the ci.yml cron the verdict names, 37123811425/37129011940/37157439771 are
the three oct3-verify attempts - so a step that reads them reads history, not a story.
Each step names its ACTOR (who might run it), the CLOCK (what day the world is having) and
what must be true afterwards. `expect.recordLine` is the record's identity AND its verdict
as one line: the text the script writes, the text the recovery pass searches for, and the
text the heartbeat audits against - all three rendered from scripts/verdict-contract.json.
tests/rehearsal-lifecycle.test.ts holds these literals to the declaration, so a rehearsal
cannot pass while a script and the loader disagree about what a record is called.

commit.message: chore: refresh node-schedule.json from nodejs.org [skip ci]

steps.name: Refresh the committed schedule snapshot from nodejs.org
Commit the refreshed snapshot with the deploy key
computed: the verifier derives the verdict and cannot file it
about: The cron day. The verifier finds the scheduled ci.yml run and the snapshot commit,
derives PASS_REFRESHED, composes the record, prints it - and the POST comes back 403,
because this workflow (and only this one) posts to #18 without `issues: write`. It exits
0 anyway: the verdict is real, so the job is green and the record is nowhere.

stdout: COMMENT_FAILED Response status code does not indicate success: 403

steps.name: filed: the workflow uploads the run log the record lives in
about: The record's only durable home: `pwsh ... | tee oct3-verify.log`, the exit line appended,
uploaded as the oct3-verify-log artifact. This step plays the workflow (the rehearsal is a
runner here, not a tool) for all three attempts, and then asks the recovery pass's own
parser to rebuild the record out of that artifact - because "recoverable" is a property of
the artifact, and nothing else about this step can establish it.
steps.from: computed: the verifier derives the verdict and cannot file it

steps.name: lost: the day-after sentinel trips on the missing receipt
about: Oct 4 01:00, the sentinel's own morning. Three scheduled attempts fired and concluded
success, and no comment on #18 carries a PASS verdict - so the sentinel does what it was
built to do: it files the gap. This is the real 2026-10-04 state.
Needs no DRY_RUN: the transport is the simulated world, which is where the trip belongs.
The clock sits seconds AFTER the run's own created_at (01:00:09) on purpose: the trip is
that run's record, and the recovery pass will not read a receipt created before the run it
belongs to (isReceipted). A world that dated the record earlier would leave the sentinel's
own run looking like a lost record, and the pass would say so - which is how this step
found that rule the first time it ran.

steps.name: lost: the auditor says the run owed a record and never recorded it
about: The same world, seen by the other witness. The auditor reads the run list: a completed
scheduled oct3-verify run started after its due slot, and the receipt contract promises a
record for that period - and there is none. It says so on #18, in its own words, and its
comment must NOT count as the record: this diary entry is the exact shape of a comment
that can satisfy a careless receipt test (the 2026-10-05 heartbeat comment quoted the
marker while reporting the record missing). The step asserts the pass still finds the run
unreceipted after the auditor has spoken.

steps.name: recovered: the pass re-posts the record from the artifact
about: The recovery pass enumerates the chain's scheduled runs inside the retention window,
finds every one of them unreceipted, reads each run's own artifact, and re-posts the
record. Three attempts computed one day's verdict, so ONE record is what may land: a
receipt recorded after a run covers that run, which is the contract's own rule and the
reason a retry chain is one comment and not three.

stdout: oct3-verify.yml: 3 scheduled run(s) inside retention, 3 without a record
oct4-sentinel.yml: 1 scheduled run(s) inside retention (only tripped runs owe a record), 0 without a record

steps.name: recovered: a second pass finds nothing left to recover
about: The pass's own idempotence, asked of the world it just changed. A record that returns and
then returns again is the duplicate-record failure this contract exists to prevent, so the
second run must post nothing at all.

stdout: oct3-verify.yml: 3 scheduled run(s) inside retention, 0 without a record

steps.name: retired: the auditor grades the trip stale and the receipt landed
about: The handoff that closes the loop. The sentinel's trip run (Oct 4 01:00) is still the
latest run for its slot, but the receipt it was waiting for landed at 12:15 - so the
auditor reports the Oct 3 verdict as recorded (naming the very comment the pass posted)
and the trip as STALE rather than re-filing a gap that is already repaired. No findings.
The world's clock moves 15 minutes and the same tools that reported two findings an hour
ago report none.

steps.name: retired: the sentinel stands down
about: And the sentinel that filed the gap, run again against the same world, finds the record
it was waiting for and stands down - naming the comment the recovery pass posted. The
script that wrote the original record, the pass that rebuilt it, and the alarm it was the
witness for all agree about one comment on one issue: that is the lifecycle.
No DRY_RUN and no fixture comment: the record it recognises is the one this run recovered.
Its comment count reads 2/PASS 1, not 1/1: the auditor's report QUOTES the verifier's
marker while saying the record is missing, and a marker is not a verdict - the PASS count
(what the sentinel actually acts on) is the one that has to be 1.

stdout: SENTINEL_OK latest PASS from run comment
